name: Jacksonville
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Jacksonville: logistics and port fraud, fintech diligence, defense contractor and asset research.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters that touch Jacksonville, the consolidated city-county at the centre of Northeast Florida and a hub for logistics, financial technology, health care and naval operations. Engagements are scoped from Nashville, with Florida-licensed professionals for any fieldwork, and focus on counterparties, disputes and assets in Northeast Florida.
intro: Jacksonville is a consolidated city-county: the governments of the city and Duval County merged in 1968, giving it a land area of about 747 square miles and, at the 2020 census, 949,611 residents in the city. The five-county metropolitan area of Baker, Clay, Duval, Nassau and St. Johns counties had about 1.73 million people at the start of 2024, according to HUD. The regional economy rests on transportation and logistics, anchored by CSX's headquarters, Crowley and JAXPORT, financial services and payments firms such as FIS and Fidelity National Financial, health care led by Baptist Health and Mayo Clinic, and a large naval presence at NAS Jacksonville and Naval Station Mayport.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Jacksonville because of the transactions its main industries generate. Freight, warehousing and port activity raise questions about cargo theft, carrier and broker fraud and the reliability of logistics partners. The concentration of payments, title insurance and banking operations creates exposure to vendor fraud, insider misconduct and disputes with former employees. Defense contractors and suppliers to the Navy need background research on subcontractors and partners. Rapid population growth has fuelled real estate and construction activity, along with disputes over development, contractors and property ownership. Lawyers handling litigation, collections and judgment enforcement in Northeast Florida also need asset and background research.

matters.title: Logistics, freight and cargo fraud
matters.text: Research supporting shippers, carriers and insurers when cargo disappears or a logistics relationship fails in the Jacksonville area, covering the history and ownership of brokers, carriers and warehouse operators, links between related companies and prior disputes, to support recovery, claims handling and counsel's litigation decisions.

matters.title: Fintech and payments counterparty diligence
matters.text: Background research on payments companies, vendors and partners connected to Jacksonville's financial technology and banking operations, examining corporate history, principals, regulatory actions, litigation and reported data incidents before vendor onboarding, partnerships, acquisitions or significant outsourcing arrangements.

matters.title: Defense supplier and subcontractor checks
matters.text: Research on subcontractors, suppliers and joint venture partners serving the naval installations and defense contractors around Jacksonville, covering ownership, foreign connections disclosed in public records, prior contract disputes, debarment and enforcement history, to support compliance and teaming decisions.

matters.title: Real estate and construction disputes
matters.text: Factual research for counsel in disputes over development projects, contractors and property in fast-growing Duval, Clay, Nassau and St. Johns counties, tracing ownership of entities behind projects, liens and recorded documents, related-party transactions and the litigation history of developers and contractors.

matters.title: Judgment enforcement and asset research
matters.text: Lawful asset and background research supporting collection and judgment enforcement against debtors in Duval and surrounding counties, using property and official records, court dockets, corporate filings and public sources, while respecting limits on access to financial and other protected records.

local_context.title: Fourth Judicial Circuit courts
local_context.text: State civil, commercial and criminal cases in Jacksonville are heard by the circuit and county courts of Florida's Fourth Judicial Circuit, which serves Duval, Clay and Nassau counties. The Duval County Clerk of Courts maintains court records. Because the circuit spans three counties of the metropolitan area, research on a Northeast Florida counterparty usually covers all three, together with St. Johns and Baker counties, which belong to other circuits.

local_context.title: Consolidated city-county government
local_context.text: Since October 1968 the City of Jacksonville and Duval County have operated as a single consolidated government covering almost the entire county. In practice this means many municipal and county functions, permits and records are handled by one government rather than separate city and county bodies and can simplify some public records research. The city and county populations differ slightly, so researchers still confirm which jurisdiction issued a given record.

local_context.title: Florida investigator licensing
local_context.text: Private investigation in Florida is licensed under Chapter 493, Florida Statutes, administered by the Division of Licensing of the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services. A private investigative agency needs a Class A licence for each location, branch offices need Class AA licences, and individuals performing investigative services need Class C licences while owning or working for a licensed agency. TDSC coordinates Florida-licensed professionals for any fieldwork in Jacksonville.

local_context.title: Port, rail and military hubs
local_context.text: JAXPORT describes itself as Florida's leading container port, and CSX runs its global headquarters from downtown Jacksonville. NAS Jacksonville, Naval Station Mayport and Blount Island Command support more than 122,000 regional jobs, according to the regional economic development organisation. These hubs concentrate freight, contracting and supply chain activity, and with it the disputes, fraud and compliance questions that lead to investigative work.

tdsc_approach: TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office in Jacksonville, but works on Northeast Florida matters as part of its domestic practice. Each engagement starts with the decision or proceeding the research supports, such as litigation in the Fourth Judicial Circuit, a logistics claim, a defense teaming decision or judgment enforcement, and identifies the counties and records involved. Research draws on Duval and neighbouring county court and official records, Florida and other state entity filings, federal dockets and enforcement releases, and published reporting. Any fieldwork in Florida is carried out by investigators licensed under Chapter 493, and work that could fall within the Fair Credit Reporting Act is identified and handled accordingly.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Jacksonville?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office, staff or address in Jacksonville. Matters touching Northeast Florida are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where an engagement requires interviews, observation or other fieldwork in Florida, TDSC coordinates investigators licensed under Chapter 493 of the Florida Statutes.

faqs.q: Which courts handle disputes in Jacksonville?
faqs.a: State civil and commercial disputes are heard by the circuit and county courts of the Fourth Judicial Circuit, which covers Duval, Clay and Nassau counties, with records maintained by the Duval County Clerk of Courts. Federal matters go to the federal courts. Counsel decides the forum, and TDSC scopes research to the court and proceeding concerned.

faqs.q: Can TDSC investigate a cargo loss involving a Jacksonville carrier?
faqs.a: TDSC can research the carrier, broker or warehouse operator involved, including corporate ownership, related companies, principals, prior claims and litigation and published regulatory actions, and help counsel or the insurer decide on recovery steps. Physical inspection, interviews or observation in Florida are handled by licensed Florida investigators within a defined scope.

faqs.q: Is a Florida licence needed for investigative work in Jacksonville?
faqs.a: Florida requires agencies offering private investigative services to hold a Class A licence and individual investigators a Class C licence under Chapter 493. Desk research using public sources is planned from Nashville, while any fieldwork in Jacksonville is carried out by appropriately licensed Florida professionals. Attorneys conducting their own work fall under separate rules.

faqs.q: Does TDSC support judgment enforcement in Duval County?
faqs.a: Yes, through lawful asset and background research for the client's counsel. This typically covers real property and recorded documents, business interests and filings, vehicles and vessels where publicly recorded, litigation and liens. TDSC does not obtain bank or other protected financial records outside legal process; discovery and court orders remain the route to such information.
